Not being satisfied by the Award dated 05.06.2024 made in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis M.C.O.P.No.7264 of 2016, the claimant herein has preferred this Civil Miscellaneous Petition for enhancement of compensation.

2. Heard Mr.F.Terry Chella Raja, learned counsel appearing for the appellant / Claimant,
Mr.M.Murali Vinoth, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondent / Transport Corporation.

sentences.text: 3. The main focus in this appeal is quantum, more specifically, in fixing the disability of the claimant.
4. At trial, claimant was examined as P.W1 and 17 documents were marked.

On the respondent side,
one witness was examined and one document is marked.
Copy of rough sketch is Ex.R1.

Disability Certificate issued by the medical board is Ex.C1.
5.

As per the medical records, Ex.P3, Ex.P4 and Ex.P5, the claimant suffered head injury, degloving injury over left thigh, degloving injury of left lower limb and injury over right leg and post-degloving injury sequalae left leg shortening.

From the treatment records, it is discernible that the claimant had taken treatment as inpatient from 21.10.2016 to 25.12.2016 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and thereafter, from 27.01.2017 to 21.02.2017 at Government Hospital, Chennai.
She was further treated as inpatient at Right Hospital, Chennai from 28.08.2017 to 01.09.2017.
During the said period, she had undergone four surgeries.
The Regional Medical Board, Killpauk Government Medical College Hospital issued disability certificate to the effect that her disability is fixed at 55%.

entities.text: Regional Medical Board, Killpauk Government Medical College Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: She was present in the Court during the advancement of arguments and from her photos, it is deducible that due to the degloving injury she suffers from loss of muscles in the left thigh.
Though her left leg is retained, it would be difficult for her to do her regular work.

Considering the nature of injuries and fractures suffered by the claimant and the effects upon her, we are of the considered view that the interest of justice will be met if the functional disability is fixed at 70% and monthly income is fixed at Rs.12,000/-.
6.
The Tribunal has based on the Aadhaar Card of the claimant has fixed her age at 44 years, which is not in dispute.

Therefore, as per the law laid down by the Hon'be Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in 2017 (2) TNMAC 609 (SC) as regards the future prospects, for the age group of person between 40 to 50 years, 25% has to be added as future prospects for computing monthly https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis income.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in 2017 (2) TNMAC 609 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. As per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Smt.Sarla verma and others vs Delhi Corporation and others, the relevant multiplier to be adopted is 14m.

entities.text: Smt.Sarla verma and others vs Delhi Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the loss of income is computed at Rs.17,64,000/- [Rs.15,000/- (Rs.12,000/- + 25% Future Prospects) x 12 x 14 x 70/100].
8.

Upon consideration of the injuries and fractures suffered by the claimant, on account of the accident and the effects upon her throughout her life, for pain and sufferings and for transportation,
an amount of Rs.25,000/- is granted under each head in addition to the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
Likewise, for extra nourishment and for loss of amenities, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is granted under each head in addition to the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
For computation of loss of income, as the multiplier method is invoked, the injured claimant is not entitled for loss of earnings.
We are of the considered view that with regard to other heads, the amounts awarded by the Tribunal appears to be reasonable and we are not inclined to interfere with the same.

Therefore, the Compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reworked and tabulated as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis given below:

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.13,62,000/- to Rs.21,68,000/- which would carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.

10. In the result,
(i) The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands partly allowed.
No costs.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (ii) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.13,62,000/- to Rs.21,68,000/-.

(iii) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount now determined by this Court i.e., Rs.21,68,000/- (less the amount already deposited if any) together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.7264 of 2016 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Chennai within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this Judgment.

(iv) On such deposit being made, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, after adjusting the amount, if any already withdrawn, by filing necessary application before the Tribunal.
(v) The claimant is directed to pay the Court fee for the enhanced compensation amount, if required.
(vi) The Tribunal below to disburse the amount upon production of the certified copy showing proof of payment of Court fee by the claimant.
